title: A personal guarantor's liability - recent legal developments
p1:
Think signing a personal guarantee is just a formality? Many business owners discover the reality only when things go wrong.

A personal guarantee can turn a company's debt into a personal financial responsibility.
p2:
A common misconception is that a guarantor is protected because they were not the primary borrower. Recent legal developments have reinforced that lenders can proceed against personal guarantors when the conditions for recovery are met.

In simple terms, if a company fails to repay a loan, the person who gave the guarantee may also be asked to pay. This liability does not automatically wait for every recovery option against the company to finish first.
p3:
This is especially significant for founders and directors who sign guarantees while raising business loans. A signature given during funding discussions can have consequences that extend beyond the company’s balance sheet.

The practical lesson: read guarantee documents carefully before signing. A personal guarantee is not just a promise of support; it can create a direct financial obligation.
conclusion: Would you check the legal impact of a personal guarantee before signing one for a business loan, or do most people underestimate this risk?
